category_edits.rationale: Across all four datasets, normalize log1p training-item counts by the 95th percentile among observed items, clamp to [0,1], then retain the square root and existing attenuation. This may reduce compression from exceptionally frequent items. Unseen items remain zero, and the existing checkpoint buffer carries the feature into prediction without architecture or predictor changes.

edits.find:
frequency_feature = np.log1p(training_counts)
    frequency_feature /= max(float(frequency_feature.max()), 1.0)
    frequency_feature = np.sqrt(frequency_feature)
edits.replace:
frequency_feature = np.log1p(training_counts)
    observed_frequency = frequency_feature[training_counts > 0.0]
    frequency_scale = (
        max(float(np.percentile(observed_frequency, 95.0)), 1.0)
        if observed_frequency.size else 1.0
    )
    frequency_feature = np.clip(frequency_feature / frequency_scale, 0.0, 1.0)
    frequency_feature = np.sqrt(frequency_feature)

change_summary: Use 95th-percentile normalization for the training-frequency input feature across all four category models, preserving square-root attenuation and checkpoint-backed inference.
